title: Why We Always See the Same Side of the Moon | Space Atlas
description: The Moon rotates once per orbit, exactly matching its trip around Earth. That match is called tidal locking. Toggle it off to compare.
ogTitle: Why Do We Always See the Same Side of the Moon?
ogDescription: Toggle tidal locking on and off and watch a marker on the Moon's surface to see exactly why we only ever see one face.
jsonldName: Why Do We Always See the Same Side of the Moon?
jsonldDescription: An interactive model comparing a tidally locked Moon to a hypothetical non-locked Moon, using a visible surface marker to show rotation relative to orbit.
